title: Becoming like God
hook: the Orthodox speak of salvation as union with God, like iron glowing in fire

segments.voice: Yesterday, justification: Abram under the stars, and a verdict received as a gift. Your line was declared right. What did you let yourself receive? Day one thousand eighty-nine.

A blacksmith pushes a bar of black iron into the coals and leaves it there. At first nothing seems to happen. Then a dull red creeps along it. Then orange. Then it glows so bright you can't tell where the fire stops and the iron begins. Pull it out, and it lights the room. Touch it, and it burns like fire. And yet it's still iron. It hasn't turned into fire. It has the fire all through it. Orthodox Christian teachers have reached for this picture when they try to say what salvation finally is. Not only a verdict. A glow. Today's word: theosis.
screen: `A BAR OF BLACK IRON IN THE COALS.`

segments.voice: Theosis is a Greek word: becoming godlike, sharing in God's own life. The Orthodox speak of salvation this way. Yesterday's courtroom asked how I can be in the right with God. This asks something else: how can I be filled with God? Day one thousand eighty met a line from the second letter of Peter, and the Orthodox build on it here. God has given promises "that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature." Partakers. Sharers. Exodus has a picture of it. Moses comes down the mountain after speaking with God, and "Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him." He didn't know. Still Moses, still a man, and shining. Here's the careful part, and Orthodox teachers are very careful about it. Becoming godlike never means becoming God. The iron never stops being iron. They distinguish God's inner being, which no creature can ever share, from God's life and light, which God pours out freely. One old saying puts it this way: what God is by nature, a person may become by grace. Where can you see this light? Orthodox Christians point to another mountain. Matthew says that when Jesus was transfigured, "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." They see that light as a glimpse of where human life is headed. And John's first letter keeps the ending open: "it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him." Western Christians have their own words for this hope, like union with God and seeing him face to face. The Orthodox name it theosis, and picture it glowing.
screen: `HIS FACE DID SHINE AS THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit near a warm light. If you can, sit by a sunny window, or light a candle, or turn toward a lamp. Settle, and breathe. Let the light fall on your face and hands. Feel the warmth on your skin. Notice that you don't have to do anything to be warmed. You just stay near. If you pray, you can simply stay near God, the way iron stays in the coals. If you don't, just let the light do its quiet work. The bell holds the time.
Theosis. The Orthodox word for salvation as union with God: sharing God's life and light, like iron glowing in fire, while staying iron.
Your line: iron in the fire. Today, stay a little longer near something that warms you: a person, a place, a few quiet minutes. Day one thousand eighty-nine.

howItsDone: Orthodox Christians speak of theosis as the goal of the Christian life, pursued through the sacraments, prayer such as the Jesus Prayer, fasting and love, and they celebrate the Transfiguration as a major feast, a sign of the light they hope to share.

original.note: Greek: becoming godlike, sharing in God's life. a word of the Greek church fathers.

notes: Iron-in-fire image: used by Origen, Maximus the Confessor, John of Damascus and others, often for the union of natures in Christ and for deification. The script says only 'Orthodox Christian teachers have reached for this picture'. Confirm refs.
'You become by grace what God is by nature, one ancient saying goes' paraphrases a line commonly attributed to Maximus the Confessor; confirm attribution before naming.
Essence/energies distinction (Palamas) simplified as 'inner being' versus 'life and light'; confirm the Orthodox Keeper is comfortable with this phrasing.
Day 1080 used Athanasius's 'became human that we might become godlike'; deliberately not repeated here. Day 1075 (image and likeness) is close in theme; check overlap once written.
'Western Christians have their own words for this hope, like union with God and seeing him face to face' (beatific vision): general; confirm fairness.
Transfiguration as a 'major feast' in howItsDone: it is one of the Twelve Great Feasts in the Orthodox calendar; no count stated. Confirm.
The fork's reveal links Peter's wish to stay to theosis; interpretive. Matthew 17:4 KJV: 'let us make here three tabernacles'.
